key_insight: By choosing a better Kraus unraveling of dephasing noise, the average trajectory magic in noisy random circuits can be reduced, but a significant fraction of trajectories still remain highly non-stabilizer and costly to simulate.
engineering_relevance: For stabilizer-based classical simulation of noisy quantum circuits, unraveling choice can lower average cost, but worst-case high-magic trajectories still set the practical bottleneck.
method: Studied quantum trajectories of Haar-random and T-doped random Clifford brickwork circuits with local dephasing noise.
Compared the canonical Pauli-jump unraveling against the full family of minimal unravelings.
Optimized two-parameter generalized measurements to minimize trajectory-averaged stabilizer Rényi entropy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the optimal state-independent unraveling reduces magic by a p-dependent factor while preserving linear scaling with system size, but leaves a broad distribution with many high-magic trajectories.
watch_item: Lower average magic does not remove rare high-magic trajectories, so simulation resources may still be dominated by tail events rather than the mean.
paper_title: Magic in quantum trajectory unravelings of noisy random quantum circuits
